- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.6) — model tends to overshoot in bullish periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.3) — model underreacts to bearish signals.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially after sharp spikes.
- After a price spike, model overcorrects downward, then undercorrects upward — exhibits oscillatory bias.
- Mean reversion bias: model often forecasts prices to revert to historical mean too quickly, ignoring sentiment-driven momentum.
- Sentiment-driven momentum amplifies forecast error — model fails to adjust horizon-specific weights when sentiment shifts sharply.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history — model overweights recent data when sentiment is volatile, leading to erratic forecasts.
